thread:
Anna: Quick follow-up from the RFC: are ephemeral private endpoints still rotating IPs every 6h by default? Observability graph shows brief drops for a handful of tenants.
Raj: Yes, default rotation is 6h for the ephemeral pool. We're seeing a race where agent route updates land slightly after the controlplane's acceptance, creating short blackholes.
Tim: Ugh. Can we emit a marker event during the swap so Console can correlate drops? Even a small nginx access tail before tear-down would help.
Maya: We could add a tiny "handoff" event in the controlplane audit feed: started/completed with minimal routing metadata. Consumers (Console, alerts) can join it with metrics.
Anna: Where should it be emitted from? Agent -> cp event queue seems easiest, but we must avoid widening the cp surface area for Private deployments.
Raj: My proposal: agent posts a signed handoff record to cp/audit. Keep fields minimal and scrub any PII. Sequence: agent posts {tenant, old_ip, new_ip, state, ts_start, ts_end}. CP stores for short retention and emits to the analytics topic.
Tim: Make it best-effort. If cp isn't reachable we must not block rotation. Agent should retry a few times then fall back to local logging if necessary.
Maya: Client plan: 3 retries with exponential backoff, then write a fallback event to local log shipping (so we can stitch later). Also add per-tenant rate limiting to avoid storms.
Anna: What about temporary DNAT/connection-preserve rules during rotation? Could preserve sessions but risky for asymmetric paths.
Raj: DNAT is risky across tenants and cloud providers. Alternative: lower DNS TTL to 30s around rotation and prefer DNS-based handoff inside the tenant VPC. Pros: less cp coupling. Cons: depends on client respect of TTL and may not help long-lived TCP sessions.
Tim: Sketch for agent emission (pseudo):
```
POST /cp/v1/tenant/handoff
Content-Type: application/json
{"tenant_id":"tid-987","old_ip":"10.1.4.5","new_ip":"10.1.9.7","state":"started","ts":"2026-03-21T12:01:02Z"}
```
Maya: Console: add a per-tenant "recent endpoint events" pane and annotate timelines with handoff markers so SREs can correlate latency/errors quickly. Also propose an alert rule: if a handoff is logged and error rate > X% within 60s, page on-call.
Anna: Action items: Raj -> PR with minimal schema + retention default 7d + security note on scrubbing. Tim -> implement best-effort emit + local fallback in agent. Maya -> mock Console UI and alert suggestions. Raj: set rate limit to 1 handoff/min per tenant (configurable) and disable for tenants that opt-out.
Tim: +1 on 7d and the rate limit. Keep payload tiny to minimize cost and cp load.
Raj: I'll open the issue and include a short threat model paragraph.
deploy-bot: Created issue #6127: "handoff-event-schema" and assigned to Raj.
Anna: Thanks, I'll paste metric traces for the affected tenants after my meeting so we can validate once the PR is ready.
